### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f02f4f63707bd05ae2186ca63babd54bfe37abcc`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f02f4f63707bd05ae2186ca63babd54bfe37abcc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5d145929f29465d35b240cad671a881d480d104c` — the merge of head `8598c1dcb77d7865c91fac5e967d1df84ed44d7d` into base `f02f4f63707bd05ae2186ca63babd54bfe37abcc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5d145929f29465d35b240cad671a881d480d104c && git checkout 5d145929f29465d35b240cad671a881d480d104c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f02f4f63707bd05ae2186ca63babd54bfe37abcc 8598c1dcb77d7865c91fac5e967d1df84ed44d7d && git checkout -B drift-repro f02f4f63707bd05ae2186ca63babd54bfe37abcc && git merge --no-ff 8598c1dcb77d7865c91fac5e967d1df84ed44d7d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f02f4f63707bd05ae2186ca63babd54bfe37abcc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f02f4f63707bd05ae2186ca63babd54bfe37abcc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `20c39a477f2487327a3dad27d283b890903a2d92`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/validate-date-text-arithmetic.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/assignment-value-envelope.test.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts (firstTypeMismatch, firstDateTextVerdict, firstDateTextCall), packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (resolver wiring, boot pull, re-sync), packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts (canonicalizeStoredFlow), packages/lint/src/flow-cel-root-scope.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-timestamp-date-only-refused.ts, 18.formula-date-text-call-refused.ts, 18.formula-date-subtraction-refused.ts, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md, AGENTS.md (pre-landing item 3). Not reviewed: .changeset/34451-flow-value-envelope-date-text.md as prose (read for ②).

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, narrowed — right as declared. Refused now, clean on `main`: a flow whose start node names an object (or a time-relative flow, its swept object), where field types for that object are in hand, carrying a CEL value envelope in `assignment` `assignments.*` or `create_record` / `update_record` `fields.*` whose source, with no `input` read and no Timestamp-typing mismatch elsewhere in it, holds one of: (a) `timestamp(record.F)` or `timestamp(previous.F)` with F a `date` field, alone or nested (`isoDate(timestamp(record.borrow_date) + duration('168h'))`); (b) a `date` or `datetime` field handed straight to a call with no overload on its text (`isoDate(record.picked_up_at)`, `record.d.getFullYear()`); (c) arithmetic on that text (`record.end_date - record.start_date`, `record.borrow_date - duration('24h')`). Codes `date-text-call-run-may-fail` and `date-text-arithmetic-run-may-fail`, error grade.
- Doors that now refuse: `@objectstack/lint` `validateStackExpressions` (`os validate`, `os build`, and every caller of `runStackExpressionPasses`, the runtime write gate among them); `registerFlow` wherever a resolver is wired, which `plugin.ts` does whenever an ObjectQL registry is present, so the boot pull, the re-sync and the clone route all throw; the stored pass (`canonicalizeStoredFlow().todos`) lists the slot. At boot the throw is caught per flow (`plugin.ts`, "failed to register flow", warn) and the whole flow stays unregistered: no crash, and no run of any branch of that flow.
- Doors that still accept, by design and stated: `registerFlow` with no resolver (a host without ObjectQL); the run-time evaluator (`evaluateValueEnvelope` calls `valueEnvelopeRefusals(envelope)` untyped, so a flow already armed in a live process runs and faults at the node as before); the save door's canonicalizer, which does not read `todos`. Right: registration's set is evaluation's plus one family, never less. Not traced: whether the field types the lint index holds and the ones the registry resolver returns are the same map for system fields; a difference would make the two doors refuse different sets on `record.created_at`-style reads.
- Stand-downs — right, and they keep the verdict from guessing: a `datetime` field under `timestamp()` stays clean (its text is an instant); a bare name, a `vars.x` read and any source reading `input` take no verdict; `type-mismatch*`, `date-arithmetic*`, `date-duration-value`, field existence, near-miss, bare-reference and the traversal arm do not reach the envelope; a text field holding a date literal is `string`, never typed as a date. A null-guarded call is still refused, correctly: the fault is on the text, not the null.
- Same verdict as the formula site — right in substance. `flowValueEnvelopeDateTextIssue` follows `typeSoundnessIssue`'s order (`firstTypeMismatch` first, then `dateTextIssue` at `record` scope, role `value`) and filters to the family, so the expression a formula field is refused for under `date-text-call` is refused here under the same check, with the same params, rewrite and shift; only the outcome arm differs. Known false negatives, all on the quiet side: a source that also carries a Timestamp-typing mismatch gets nothing at all here (a formula site reports the mismatch), and arithmetic beside an undeclared flow variable may fail the typed check for another reason and return null.
- Public surface, widened — right: `ExprSchemaHint` is exported from `@objectstack/formula` alone (`src/index.ts`), no spec path; one optional key, absent means byte-identical behaviour. `valueEnvelopeRefusals` gains an optional second parameter on a private method and an internal module function: not published.
- Behaviour contract of an exported type, changed — right to declare breaking: `FlowObjectSchemaResolver` promised on `main` that a resolver can never break a flow that used to register cleanly; the three amended docblocks now name the one exception.

### ② Semver level

- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the right kind (a value an author could write is refused), and AGENTS.md pre-landing item 3 gives a kind at least `minor` on each package the diff moves: `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation` are all `minor`. Correct; no package the diff moves is missing, and no spec bump is owed because no spec path moves.
- The changeset carries both declaration lines, the BREAKING banner, the FROM to TO table, the one-line fix and exactly one ADR-0087 marker. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` concluded success on this head.
- Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — matches the diff, and the widening half (one optional key on `ExprSchemaHint`) is named beside it in both the PR body and the changeset. The claim correction on the card (from `no` / `none`) was the right correction.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head: no failure concluded. Concluded success: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint ESLint, Lint docs and code guards, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Type Check source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate. Pending when read: Build Core, Test Core 1 to 8 of 8, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check debt ledger, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint scoped slot lookup and corpus, the UI shards. The gate verdicts for those families are therefore not yet given; this record judges the contract, and a red conclusion on any of them stands over it.
- Dev flag, the outcome clause says "condition": confirmed in `dateArmFault`. The refusal an author reads at a value slot says the fault happens "when the condition runs" and that "the flow stops at this condition". The outcome it states is true for a value envelope (`evaluateValueEnvelope` throws); the noun is wrong. See N1. A value-worded arm is a new refusal code: the seat's call, a follow-up card.
- Dev flag, bare names stand down: accepted. The engine door cannot see declared variables or open binders, and the two doors must refuse one set.
- Dev flag, `date-duration-value` stays out: accepted, route A names the date-text family alone.
- Dev flag, ADR-0087 `surface` prose does not name value envelopes: answered in ④, S1.
- Dev flag, found on the way (a flow CONDITION does not type `record.FIELD` reads for the date-text check, so `timestamp(record.borrow_date)` passes in a start condition while the same read is now refused in a value envelope): escalated to the seat as its own card. It is a gap on `main`, not introduced here, but after this PR the two sites of one flow disagree about one read.
- Deviation, three `engine.ts` docblocks amended: accepted, the change made them false. The sibling comment was missed, see N2.
- `Skills-docs: none`: holds. `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` states the `timestamp()` and `date-text-call` rule with no site, so it is true of value envelopes as written.
- `ExprSchemaHint.flowValueEnvelope`: the key is needed (field types on a `value` role with no flag is the formula-field path, so a mode marker is the only way to ask for the one family) and is placed beside its siblings `timeRelativeSweep`, `traversalHydration`, `bareNamesUnproven`. The NAME awaits the seat; this record does not rule on it.
- ADR-0087 disposition and stored flows at boot: answered in ④, S1.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; it is authoring-time and registration-time typing of expression text.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes a published refusal real; it takes no declared capability away. Nothing on `main` declares that `timestamp()` over a `date` field works: `SKILL.md` says it is refused, the three semantic entries say every door should have refused it, and the evaluator faults on the `YYYY-MM-DD` text at the very slot the card measured (cloud#4717). The value envelope is evaluated by the same engine on the same record values as a flow condition, and a faulting envelope throws and fails the run, so refusing it at authoring and at registration is the rule arriving at a site it had not reached. The stand-down set is conservative, the controls pin the `datetime` and non-family cases at all three layers, and both doors pass one hint. Two points do not hold as written:

S1 (should-fix) — the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (already-registered …)` claims the three entries cover this change, and they cover it only in part. ADR-0087 itself says the gate checks that the ids resolve and pre-date the base, never that the entry covers the change, and that a narrowing's upgrade notice lives in the ledger so an author learns it "before a save door, a publish or a boot refuses it". The three entries' `surface` enumerates a formula field's expression and CEL predicates (validation conditions, field rule predicates, flow conditions); a flow value envelope is neither, and their `reason` knows no outcome where a stored flow stops registering at boot, which is new with this PR and stronger than anything they describe (a flow condition with the same fault is still only a logged advisory at `registerFlow`). What does carry over is real: the codes, the rewrites, and site-free acceptance criteria (`os validate` reports no `date-text-call` finding), plus the stored pass listing the slot. So the disposition is defensible only once the ledger says so: amend the three `surface` strings to name flow value envelopes and the registration refusal (a `packages/spec/src` edit, outside this claim's surface, Tier H), or register one semantic entry for the site, or have the seat rule in writing that the site-free acceptance criteria are the coverage. The dev reported the gap; the marker's own sentence should not assert more than is true until one of those lands.

S2 (should-fix) — the refusal is fatal at `registerFlow` on a premise the engine's own contract denies. The new `ExprSchemaHint.flowValueEnvelope` docblock says the `record.FIELD` and `previous.FIELD` reads "hold the bound row's value by construction". `celScope`'s docblock on `main` says otherwise: `record` resolves through the variable spread, so it is the trigger row only when a record-change trigger or a sweep handed it; it is the request body on an inbound hook, the parent's record in a `subflow` / `map` child, and whatever the flow itself bound when it declares or assigns a variable named `record` (not a claimed identifier in `FLOW_SCOPE_CLAIMED_IDENTIFIERS`). Both doors type the envelope from the start node's `objectName` whatever the trigger kind, and the verdict's own arm is `run-may-fail`. On `main` that uncertainty is why the lint ledger declares a proven outcome only for record-triggered flows and typed sweeps, and why the engine keeps the whole resolver pass advisory. Here a flow whose `record.F` holds a full instant by one of those routes evaluates today and stops registering after the upgrade, with a warn line as the only trace. No new test covers a flow that is not record-triggered or swept. Either stand the verdict down at both doors unless the trigger binding is a record trigger or a sweep of the typed object and the flow binds no `record` of its own (the engine has `deriveTriggerBinding` in hand, lint has `triggerKind` and `flowCelRootScope`), with a CONTROL for each; or have the seat accept the residue in writing and correct the "by construction" sentence in that docblock.

N1 (nit) — the `-run-may-fail` clause names a condition at a value slot (dev-reported). Accepted deviation on this head; follow-up card for a value-worded arm.
N2 (nit) — `plugin.ts`, at the `setObjectSchemaResolver` wiring, still says "Everything it surfaces is advisory (logged, never thrown)", and its debug line says flow conditions are checked; both are now incomplete in the same way the three amended `engine.ts` docblocks were. Not in the diff; follow-up.
N3 (nit) — with `flowValueEnvelope: true` and a role other than `value`, or no `fieldTypes`, `validateExpression` runs no schema-aware pass at all and says nothing. The docblock says "`value` role only"; no caller does this today. Left as is.
N4 (nit) — on a time-relative flow whose start names a different object than it sweeps, lint types the envelope with the start object and the engine with the swept one. The publish rule `flow-time-relative-object-mismatch` already refuses that flow, and conditions have the same split on `main`. Left as is.

### ① Derived judgments

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head. Concluded failure: `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`, in its two newest runs (the first run on this head, before the PR body gained its second closing line, concluded success). The failing step is `check:closing-target-claim`: the PR closes #34661 and that card carries no `Claim:` naming `claude/project-thread-wlvkf3`. This is a red gate verdict on the head; nothing in the tree can clear it, the card or the PR body must. It stands over this record until green. It cannot refuse a flow that evaluates today on any declared screen input: before the screen runs `record` is the trigger row and the fault is real, and after it `record` is the submitted value, on which a member read yields no instant.
